passages.provision_quote: any application for registration shall be accompanied by satisfactory evidence of citizenship as prescribed in section 16-166, subsection F, and the county recorder or other officer in charge of elections shall reject any application for registration that is not accompanied by satisfactory evidence of citizenship
passages.note: Chaptered text of the bill Nguyen co-sponsored and voted for; it prints the provision but names no voter.
Bill overview lists Nguyen as a co-sponsor; it prints no provision text and no tally.
House Third Reading vote page names Nguyen as a Y and prints the count; 26 of 60 against, so not near-unanimous.

rows.reasoning: Nguyen co-sponsored HB2492 (2022) and voted Y on House Third Reading, which passed 31-26, so the vote is not near-unanimous. The bill is single-subject on qualification and registration of electors, and its operative section requires that "any application for registration shall be accompanied by satisfactory evidence of citizenship" and that the recorder "shall reject any application for registration that is not accompanied by satisfactory evidence of citizenship." That matches both clauses of the rung requiring documentary proof of citizenship to register to vote — the demand is a citizenship document, and it falls at registration rather than at the polls.
